historical_change: The viewpoint shifts from Riemann's inversion formula for a weighted prime count to Weil/Bombieri's test-function dictionary, where the same prime-zero bridge is organized as a local/global identity.
limits: The shared move is translation, not simplification: after crossing the dictionary one still has to control the zero-side oscillation or the prime-side error term. Bombieri's geometric trace reading is exact only in the function-field analogue, and AIM's unit is an overview map rather than a new proof route.
quality_reason: Accepted because all three units explicitly use a prime-zero dictionary and keep the remaining proof burden visible.
synthesis: Riemann turns the Euler product into a weighted prime-power counting object and recovers it by Mellin-style inversion of log zeta. Bombieri recasts the same bridge as Weil's explicit formula, where one test function is read simultaneously on the zero side and the prime-power side, and in the function-field case as a Frobenius trace formula. AIM then uses that fixed dictionary to list prime-counting error terms and zero-location statements as equivalent formulations of the Riemann Hypothesis.
title: Explicit-Formula Translation Between Primes and Zeros

historical_change: The criterion language moves from arithmetic inequalities to Hilbert-space closure and positivity functionals, but the change is representational rather than an escape from RH's hardness.
limits: These are relocations of difficulty, not easier proofs. The Lagarias and Baez-Duarte criteria remain all-n or full-closure statements, and Conrey's unit is explicit that the positivity formulation still has an interpretive gap.
quality_reason: Accepted because each unit replaces zero-location language by an equivalent problem and names where the full difficulty reappears.
synthesis: Lagarias turns the Riemann Hypothesis into an elementary-looking divisor-sum inequality while stating that the hard work is still carried by Robin's deeper criterion. Baez-Duarte sharpens Nyman-Beurling by asking for the same closure statement inside the thinner natural-number subfamily B_nat, so zero-location language becomes a Hilbert-space approximation problem without losing the global burden. Conrey then rewrites Weil's explicit formula as positivity, first for an admissible functional and then for Li's discrete sequence, while saying openly that the source still lacks a natural explanation for that positivity.
title: Equivalent Criteria Repackage Rather Than Solve RH

historical_change: The viewpoint changes from a conditional probe of zero spacings to a broader program that imports random-matrix calculations after an explicit scale-matching step.
limits: The common structure is local statistical transfer, not an exact identification of zeta with a matrix model. Montgomery's theorem is range-limited, and Keating-Snaith explicitly keep finite-height arithmetic corrections separate from the universal random-matrix term.
quality_reason: Accepted because the units align tightly on scale normalization, symmetry-class selection, and the need to keep arithmetic corrections visible.
synthesis: Montgomery studies zero spacings through a Fourier/form-factor observable and proves the random-matrix-looking behavior only on the restricted range below the frequency break. His conjectural continuation and Dyson's comparison then pick the unitary/Hermitian symmetry class and exclude neighboring real-symmetric and symplectic alternatives. Keating and Snaith extend that local transfer to zeta values by matching the mean-spacing scale with matrix size and then splitting the finite-height story into a universal CUE term plus a separate arithmetic correction built from primes.
title: Random-Matrix Transfer of Local Zero Statistics

historical_change: The viewpoint moves from local machine diagnosis of doubtful intervals and Gram-law failures to reproducible finite certification with an explicit completeness layer and labeled downstream consequences.
limits: The shared structure is the boundary between local detection and exhaustive accounting, not a general claim that computation proves RH. Lehmer's unit is exploratory local diagnosis without an explicit completeness theorem, and even the modern verified result remains finite-height evidence with bounded downstream reach.
quality_reason: Accepted because the revised synthesis keeps Lehmer as a pre-completeness contrast and makes Platt-Trudgian's completeness mechanism the actual anchor.
synthesis: Lehmer's SWAC computation separates ordinary Gram intervals from doubtful or failed cases, then uses subdivision and later higher-accuracy follow-up programs to inspect those local irregularities more closely. Platt and Trudgian make explicit what that older span does not supply: sign changes on the critical line must be paired with a Turing-method zero count and rigorous numerical error control to certify that every expected zero in a finite height range has been found. Their second unit then shows what such finite certification can legitimately propagate to explicit bounds, while also marking which advertised gains are only slight or future.
title: Finite Verification Needs Completeness, Not Just Computation

limits: All three sources make zero behavior legible only after moving to an ambient structured observable, but that commonality is still too broad here. Bombieri's unit is an analogical geometric realization for one function-field zeta function, whereas the other two are family-averaged low-lying-zero statistics; the linked units do not state one source-tight operative mechanism beyond that umbrella.
quality_reason: Quarantined because the current unit set mixes geometric analogy with family-density classification and would need different units or a tighter title to become training-facing.
synthesis: Bombieri packages the zeros and poles of a function-field zeta function as Frobenius eigenvalues on cohomology, making the analogue of RH part of a geometric dictionary. Rubinstein instead compresses low-lying zeros from whole L-function families into one-level densities ordered by conductor and matched to orthogonal symmetry templates. Miller keeps the same family-level observable but separates the universal symplectic main term from explicit arithmetic lower-order corrections.
title: L-Function Families Turn Single Objects into Symmetry Classes

audit_reconciliation.reason: Rejected after blinded independent audit: the three units share only a loose physical re-encoding umbrella, and the zeta-state unit does not carry the RH-level mechanism.

historical_change: The emphasis shifts from an open spectral program to more concrete physical observables, while the decisive analytic burden remains in the trace formula or equivalent criterion rather than in the new language itself.
limits: What is shared is re-encoding zeta data into another observable, not a common proof method. Only Connes and the Veneziano criterion speak directly to RH-level zero or phase constraints; the zeta-state unit is a representation-with-barrier result that does not itself control zero statistics.
quality_reason: Rejected after blinded independent audit: the three units share only a loose physical re-encoding umbrella, and the zeta-state unit does not carry the RH-level mechanism.
synthesis: Connes recasts zeta zeros as an absorption spectrum on an adele-class space and makes the missing global trace formula, not the local spectral pieces, the decisive open step. The entanglement paper realizes the Dirichlet representation itself as an overlap amplitude and translates the sigma = 1 convergence barrier into a physical conservation constraint on the implementation. The Veneziano paper rewrites the Riemann Hypothesis into the phase of a dressed amplitude, giving an exact integral criterion rather than a new derivation.
title: Physical and Spectral Re-encodings of Zeta

audit_reconciliation.reason: Accepted after blinded independent audit: the first three units share a mollifier/admissibility mechanism, while the Harper unit is explicitly retained as a boundary mismatch rather than presented as another instance.

limits: With these exact units the candidate splits in two. Conrey and Bui support a coherent mollifier-and-admissibility synthesis, but Harper's clipped span is an indirect moment-to-log-distribution reformulation rather than another tunable-weight zero-proportion argument.
quality_reason: Accepted after blinded independent audit: the first three units share a mollifier/admissibility mechanism, while the Harper unit is explicitly retained as a boundary mismatch rather than presented as another instance.
synthesis: Conrey's two units make the zero-proportion method depend on a tunable surrogate: a longer mollifier becomes usable only after analytic reduction, arithmetic main-term control, and Kloosterman-sum error bounds are assembled, and the polynomial or derivative combination is left adjustable. Bui sharpens the same point by treating admissible mollifier lengths and cross terms as substantive mathematical constraints rather than bookkeeping. Harper's linked unit, however, only rewrites a moment integral as an exponential average of log |zeta|; in this exact span it does not participate in the mollifier-admissibility mechanism claimed by the candidate.
title: Auxiliary Weights Become the Real Optimization Problem

historical_change: The viewpoint moves from counting how many bad zeros can occur to splicing several explicit nonvanishing mechanisms into a piecewise best exclusion package.
limits: These sources share edge-of-strip exclusion logic, not a route to the critical line. Zero-density estimates and zero-free regions are different exclusion modes, and the modern explicit gains remain highly sensitive to constants, height ranges, and auxiliary optimization choices.
quality_reason: Accepted because the exclusion mechanism is concrete in every source and the limits remain mathematically substantive.
synthesis: Jutila converts zero-density control into a large-values counting problem for Dirichlet polynomials and then uses those counts to limit how many zeros can occupy a region. The 2000 zero-free-region unit instead turns Vinogradov-Korobov-type growth control into an explicit forbidden region near sigma = 1. The 2024 comparison paper keeps the same partial-result aim but makes the method modular, splicing trigonometric-polynomial choices, improved growth bounds, verified RH heights, and intermediate comparisons into a height-dependent best region.
title: Partial Results by Excluding or Diluting Bad Zeros

historical_change: A spacing statistic first used as a conjectural description of the zeros becomes the obstruction that rules out an entire deformation scenario for them.
limits: The contradiction is not generated by heat flow alone. The deformation argument still depends on importing external zero-statistics information, so the method relocates the proof burden to dynamical control plus a non-equilibrium input.
quality_reason: Accepted because the Rodgers-Tao units explicitly use Montgomery-type local statistics as the contradiction endpoint.
synthesis: Rodgers and Tao embed the zero problem into the backward-heat-flow family H_t and isolate the threshold Lambda separating all-real and non-real regimes. Their proof-strategy unit then says that a negative Lambda would force the zeros of H_0 toward local arithmetic-progression equilibrium through repulsion and energy monotonicity. Montgomery supplies the incompatible comparison object: the zeta zeros are conjecturally governed by unitary-type local statistics, not by the rigid near-equilibrium spacing that the negative-Lambda scenario would impose.
title: Heat Flow Turns Zero Statistics into an Obstruction

limits: These are three different analytic moves tied to three different observables. Exceptional-set prime control, Jensen-function zero frequencies, and mesoscopic Gaussian fluctuations do not yield one concrete source-tight shared mechanism beyond the generic fact that they are not pointwise theorems.
quality_reason: Rejected because the candidate collapses distinct averaging frameworks into teacher-template abstraction rather than a reusable mathematical move.
synthesis: Gallagher replaces a pointwise prime-number-theorem remainder by an exceptional-set statement backed by mean-square control. The generalized-almost-periodicity unit turns mean motions and strip-zero frequencies of log zeta(s)-x and zeta(s)-x into derivatives of a Jensen function. The mesoscopic fluctuation unit compresses nearby log zeta values into a Gaussian field whose covariance depends only on relative shift scales.
title: Almost-Everywhere Control Replaces Pointwise Ambition

limits: Each unit is a genuine representation change, but the three do not share one conserved object or one common operative mechanism. As linked here, the candidate is mainly a chronological tour from inversion to statistics to spectrum.
quality_reason: Rejected because 'representation change exposes hidden regularity' is too broad to function as evidence-backed synthesis for these exact units.
synthesis: Riemann uses Mellin inversion to reconstruct a weighted prime-power count from log zeta. Montgomery uses a conjecturally extended pair-correlation observable to classify the zeros statistically by the unitary symmetry class. Connes proposes an absorption-spectrum and trace-formula program on adele classes.
title: From Analytic Inversion to Statistical and Spectral Viewpoints

historical_change: The failure mode shifts from outright false sufficient conditions to later analogy stress tests that retain diagnostic constraints while discarding literal proof claims.
limits: These are not failures of one severity. Some routes are falsified, others are artefactual or incomplete; the common lesson is narrower and more useful than 'spectral ideas fail': a translated representation is only informative if the exact sign, positivity, and multiplicity obligations survive the translation.
quality_reason: Accepted because every unit names a concrete mismatch or falsified premise at the point where decisive control should have appeared.
synthesis: AIM gives the sharpest failure form: Turan-type zero-free conditions for partial sums and a de Branges-type positivity route would imply the Riemann Hypothesis, but the proposed auxiliary statements are themselves false. Conrey's spectral anecdote shows a softer collapse, where apparently decisive Laplacian eigenvalues were traced to pseudo cusp forms and computation artefact. Connes's periodic-orbit comparison keeps the analogy only as a constraint list, because the sign and finite-repeat mismatches show that the semiclassical picture does not yet carry the exact arithmetic burden of the Euler product.
title: When Attractive Representations Lose the Decisive Step

historical_change: The viewpoint moves from excluding derivative zeros in explicit regions to treating the derivative ladder as an argument-principle system whose boundary data controls later zero counts.
limits: The shared role is a derivative interface, not a full unconditional proof package. Spira's unit is partly computational and OCR-limited, the inheritance theorem only propagates specific finiteness information, and Ki's count extraction is RH-conditional.
quality_reason: Accepted because all three units use derivative-side interface objects to relocate zero control, and the revised synthesis keeps the conditional and OCR-limited boundaries explicit.
synthesis: Spira first turns the search for zeros of zeta' into a region-by-region feasibility problem, where reflected functional-equation estimates and monotonicity can exclude left-side zeros in explicit ranges. Levinson and Montgomery then make the transfer mechanism explicit: a finiteness statement for left-of-half-line zeros of zeta^(m) forces zeta^(m+1) to stay zero-free there because the real-zero part of zeta^(m+1)/zeta^(m) dominates the remainder. Ki closes the loop at the counting level under RH by reducing N_k(T) to critical-line endpoint arguments, so derivative zero information is read off from boundary variation rather than from direct root location.
title: Derivative Zeros as a Relocated RH Interface

historical_change: The viewpoint shifts from a heuristic thin-set prediction to explicit subsequence and forcing rules that move any extremal witness onto more rigid abundant-number scaffolding.
limits: Lagarias's transfer from prime excess to divisor-sum excess is heuristic in this span, and the XA-to-CA forcing result only activates after an extremal witness already exists. These units localize plausible witnesses; they do not produce a counterexample or prove RH.
quality_reason: Accepted because the exact units all support witness localization onto thin extremal sets plus endpoint transport, without inflating the claim into a generic equivalent-criterion story.
synthesis: Lagarias argues that RH-sensitive excess in sigma(n)/n should be searched for on colossally abundant numbers, because prime-distribution fluctuations are amplified there and any counterexamples should be sparse and huge. Nazardonyavi and Yakubovich then put Robin's criterion and Gronwall's envelope on the same normalized scale f(n), which turns an all-integers inequality into an extremal search problem on abundant subsequences. Their CA-to-XA transfer step adds the missing transport rule: once an extremely abundant witness appears between consecutive colossally abundant numbers, the upper endpoint is forced into the witness class as well. The shared role is not another equivalence map but a carrier-set mechanism for where RH-sensitive arithmetic evidence can live and how it propagates.
title: Extremal Abundance Subsequences as RH Witness Carriers

historical_change: The viewpoint changes from one specially engineered explicit-formula kernel to an explicit Hilbert-space extremal geometry for admissible test functions.
limits: These are bounding interfaces, not equivalence criteria. The method only controls observables compatible with the chosen Fourier support and approximation cost, so sharper kernels require sharper admissibility tradeoffs rather than a free gain.
quality_reason: Accepted because each linked span explicitly replaces a hard observable by an admissible majorant, minorant, or kernel with a named approximation cost.
synthesis: Carneiro, Chandee, and Milinovich choose bandlimited surrogates for arctan(1/x)-x/(1+x^2), insert them into the explicit formula, and keep the zero sum, gamma term, and prime-power term simultaneously tractable in bounds for S(t). Carneiro, Littmann, and Vaaler do the same style of engineering for interval indicators in pair correlation: Beurling-Selberg majorants quantify the unavoidable smoothing cost, and the reproducing-kernel reformulation moves the extremal question into Hilbert-space geometry where orthogonality identifies the optimizer. Across both sources, the mathematical role is to pay a controlled approximation price in exchange for a test function the global formula can actually digest.
title: Bandlimited Surrogates Turn Zero Sums into Optimization Problems

historical_change: The computational viewpoint moves from one-shot smoothed expansions to multi-stage phase-aware descent, where each transformation is justified by the geometry of the oscillation.
limits: These units improve evaluability rather than logical strength. Smoothing creates its own correction tradeoff, recursive descent depends on parameter regimes, and none of the three units certifies completeness or proves RH.
quality_reason: Accepted because the exact spans all make tractability come from transformed oscillatory representations with explicit costs, stopping rules, or regime restrictions.
synthesis: Rubinstein's smoothed Gram-type formula simplifies the main Dirichlet sum by adding exponential damping, but also makes the hidden cost explicit: the correction series forces a Gram-scale cutoff and a nontrivial choice of truncation index. Hiary's first phase likewise classifies cubic sums by phase geometry, demoting saddle-free pieces to quadratic problems and isolating the genuinely hard middle regime. The second phase then repeatedly shortens the quadratic object itself, with stopping rules dictated by when the transformed parameters cease to help. The shared role is algorithmic re-encoding of oscillation, not better theorems about zeros.
title: Oscillatory Zeta Evaluation via Smoothing and Degree Reduction

historical_change: The viewpoint shifts from a statistical law about zero differences to a structured machine for extracting concrete prime-gap or prime-pair consequences.
limits: The bridge is not fully rigid. Montgomery's large-alpha step is heuristic, Mueller's argument is existence-through-averaging rather than uniform positivity, and the stronger decomposition still depends on conjectural pair-correlation structure.
quality_reason: Accepted because all three units keep the observable-to-arithmetic transport explicit, and the synthesis does not blur conjectural pair-correlation input into a proved prime theorem.
synthesis: Montgomery's heuristic continuation of the form factor beyond the proved small-alpha range turns zero spacing into a conjectural pair-correlation law. Mueller then uses averaged positivity rather than pointwise control: after weighting over shifts, one concrete shift survives, and that surviving positivity is converted into the existence of nearby primes. Goldston and Montgomery refine the same channel by splitting the correlation statistic into named terms whose different logarithmic and integral contributions can be tracked separately, making the prime-side transfer sensitive to more than one bulk asymptotic. The shared role is downstream transport from zero statistics to prime-pattern evidence.
title: Pair Correlation as a Transport Channel Back to Primes

historical_change: The viewpoint moves from mollified positive-proportion theorems for Dirichlet characters to a broader family-averaging architecture in which contour localization, zero-density bounds, and explicit-formula averaging extract many good twists while quantifying the obstructing ones.
limits: The conclusions are family-level and not constructive. Michel-VanderKam's slices give fixed-point nonvanishing and absence of real zeros on a segment for positive proportions of characters, while Perelli-Pomykala's slices concern average-rank and zero-density extraction for elliptic twists rather than a second direct nonvanishing theorem. All four units depend on averaged inputs, and the elliptic-twist side still needs explicit-formula and density control to manage the bad set.
quality_reason: Accepted after narrowing the claim to family-averaged extraction: the Dirichlet-character units provide direct nonvanishing and no-real-zero proportions, and the elliptic-twist units contribute the same supply-versus-obstruction logic at the level of average rank rather than another blanket nonvanishing statement.
synthesis: Michel and VanderKam show two versions of family-level extraction for Dirichlet characters. At a fixed point, a mollified first moment and controlled second moment force a positive proportion of characters to satisfy L(a,chi) != 0; on a whole interval, short interval covering and Cauchy-integral localization convert the existence of a real zero into an averaged contour count, yielding a positive proportion with no real zero in the stated strip. Perelli and Pomykała use the same supply-versus-obstruction logic for quadratic twists of an elliptic curve, but with a different output variable: moment information creates a supply of useful twists, zero-density estimates limit how many can be spoiled by bad zero configurations, and Weil's explicit formula rewrites the remaining average-rank burden as the arithmetic correction term S(lambda,d). The shared role is not blanket nonvanishing. It is extraction of many good family members by comparing total supply against averaged obstructions rather than solving any individual L-function outright.
title: Family Averaging Extracts Many Good Members While Rationing Bad Ones

historical_change: The viewpoint shifts from a failed finite approximation to a weighted, zero-expanded picture where trend and oscillation are deliberately separated.
limits: These units do not turn the criterion into an easy test. The repaired approximation is still delicate, the visible first-zero wave is descriptive rather than decisive, and the weighted sums control presentation more than they settle RH.
quality_reason: Accepted because the linked units all stabilize a delicate criterion by weighting or decomposition and then isolate the meaningful behavior as zero-driven oscillation.
synthesis: Baez-Duarte shows why natural finite approximants fail in the needed Hilbert norm and repairs the route by replacing finite cutoff with analytic weighting across the full range of scales. Beltraminelli, Merlini, and Vega then make the same criterion family computationally legible by expanding R(x) and c_k in zero sums whose first mode dominates the visible wave, and by showing that alternating or Abel-type weighting converges where raw summation does not. Wolf sharpens the interpretive split by separating a smooth k^-2 trend from the genuinely interesting zero-indexed oscillation. The common role is not another equivalence statement but a stabilization-and-frequency decomposition of a fragile criterion.
title: Discrete RH Criteria Become Zero-Driven Oscillation Problems

historical_change: The viewpoint moves from analytic continuation of a global multi-zeta object to a finer correlation language where the same moment is recovered from diagonal matching, Type II parameterization, and symmetry quotienting.
limits: These units supply architecture, not final moment asymptotics on their own. Continuation, swap matching, and automorphism correction still leave hard off-diagonal estimation and convergence issues to later work.
quality_reason: Accepted because all four units explicitly unpack moment calculations into identifiable bookkeeping objects instead of treating the analytic residue as a black box.
synthesis: Brubaker, Bump, Friedberg, and Hoffstein begin by concentrating the analytic hazard of a moment problem into a multiple Dirichlet kernel with controlled continuation and pole structure. Conrey and Keating then show, from the ascending coefficient side, that the diagonal part of a zeta moment matches the same zeta-factor object that appears in the swap recipe. In the later Type II analysis, near multiplicative equalities are turned into small additive defects via Farey-style parameters, and the apparent overcounting is finally reinterpreted as genuine automorphism multiplicity rather than an error. The shared role is structural unpacking of moments into a quotientable combinatorial geometry.
title: Moment Problems Are Repackaged as Correlation and Symmetry Bookkeeping
